title: 12 Axes
description: A quiz of 240 questions to estimate your position on the 12 political axes.

questions.text: States and cities should be able to defy federal government decisions when the local population disagrees.
The whole country should follow the same laws, even against the preferences of each state.
Taxes and public services should be decided as close to the local population as possible.
A single national school curriculum is better than each state teaching its own way.
Each state should have its own constitution, its own laws, and its own police.
A single national police force would work better than several autonomous state police forces.
Most taxes should stay in the state or city where they were collected.
Healthcare, education, and security should follow strong national command.
States should have the right to secede from the country if the local majority votes for it.
Tax competition between states shows that taxes should be set at the national level.
Indigenous and traditional communities should be able to live under their own rules within their territories.
Labor laws should be the same across the whole country, without local negotiations.
Cities should be able to create their own laws, even ones different from national laws.
When a governor and the president clash, the final word should belong to the president.
My country would work better as a union of nearly independent states.
The federal government should be able to overturn state and local laws that go against the national interest.
Regions with a strong cultural identity should have more political autonomy.
Separatist movements should be treated as a crime against the unity of the country.
Education and healthcare work better when run by local governments than by the national capital.
Governors and mayors should simply carry out the central government's orders.
Free elections must be kept even when they elect bad governments.
In serious crises, a strong leader should be able to govern without depending on the legislature.
The press, the opposition, and protests must be able to harshly criticize any government.
Most voters vote without understanding the issues that are at stake.
Constitutional courts, such as a supreme court, should be able to strike down majority-backed laws that violate the constitution.
A country advances more with a competent leader than with hotly contested elections all the time.
Secret and universal suffrage is non-negotiable, even for poorly informed voters.
A ruler who delivers results deserves to stay in power for as long as they are capable.
The people should be able to overturn laws by referendum, without depending on the legislature.
A monarchy can give a country more stability than constant elections.
Voters should be able to remove a bad politician from office before the end of the term.
Some dictatorships developed their countries faster than many democracies.
Public offices could be assigned by lottery among ordinary citizens, like a jury, instead of elected.
A government of experts chosen by merit would be better than elected politicians.
No one should govern without having gone through the popular vote.
The right to vote should be restricted; not every adult should be allowed to vote.
A society organized by assemblies, without professional rulers, could work.
Deep reforms take time and should not be interrupted by frequent elections.
Even a government elected by a huge majority must respect all the rights of the opposition.
A dictatorship can be legitimate if it guarantees order, security, and prosperity.
In areas dominated by crime, tough police operations and neighborhood-wide search warrants are acceptable.
Marijuana should be legalized for production, sale, and use among adults.
The state should be able to monitor digital conversations to prevent terrorism and organized crime.
Freedom of speech must apply even to extremist and offensive ideas.
Facial recognition cameras in the streets should be expanded to reduce crime.
What adults do among themselves — drugs, gambling, prostitution — should not be a police matter.
The state should be able to ban parties and groups that threaten public order.
All drugs, including cocaine, should be legalized for adults.
Civilian access to firearms should be severely restricted by law.
Law-abiding citizens should be able to use guns to defend their home and family.
In serious situations, curfews and states of emergency are legitimate tools.
Voluntary euthanasia should be legalized for people suffering from terminal illnesses.
Vaccination should be mandatory, even against the will of those who refuse.
It is better to let a guilty person go free than to convict an innocent one.
The death penalty should be adopted for crimes such as rape and murder.
Any law that bans what adults do in private is an abuse by the state.
The government should be able to take down websites and profiles that spread fake news.
Instant digital payment systems give the government a dangerous power to monitor every purchase.
Terrorism suspects should be held without trial until the threat has passed.
No one should be forced to unlock their phone for the police.
Those who immigrate to a country should learn the language and adopt local customs.
A multicultural society should live with several languages in everyday life.
Closing the borders may be necessary to preserve a country's cultural identity.
A society that welcomes different customs becomes richer and more creative.
Some cultures and peoples have customs incompatible with a free society.
Immigrants should not have to abandon their customs to live well in the country.
Preserving national traditions matters more than accommodating foreign customs.
The mix of languages and cultures in the same territory is a sign of progress, not crisis.
Countries have the right to prefer immigrants from cultures similar to their own.
The cultures brought by peoples from other continents are part of my country's identity.
Requiring immigrants to adapt to the local culture is not prejudice; it is a condition for living together.
My country does the right thing by taking in refugees from neighboring countries in crisis.
A people that loses its language and customs ceases to exist as a nation.
Judging an entire culture as backward or dangerous is prejudice, not an argument.
Immigrant neighborhoods that live closed off in their own culture create problems for the country.
Children of immigrants should also be able to study in their parents' language, in bilingual schools.
Ideally, each people would live separately in its own territory, without mixing cultures.
Borders should be open: any peaceful person could live in any country.
Illegal immigrants should face mass deportation, with no exceptions.
The idea of national identity is outdated: we are all citizens of the world.
A country is only respected in the world if it has strong armed forces.
Negotiation and diplomacy must be exhausted before any military action.
Preemptive strikes are acceptable against enemies preparing to attack.
Wars are almost never worth it, even against hostile regimes.
Heavy defense spending is necessary, even with other areas needing the money.
Smart diplomacy prevents more conflicts than a heavy military arsenal.
My country should pursue nuclear weapons so as not to depend on any power's protection.
The more countries spend on weapons, the greater the risk of war for everyone.
Mandatory military service makes citizens more disciplined and patriotic.
Disarmament agreements do more for peace than arms races.
The country should have its own arms industry, not depend on buying from abroad.
No political or ideological cause justifies starting a war.
Espionage and covert military operations are legitimate tools of a state.
International courts should judge war crimes, including those of allied countries.
Drones and autonomous weapons provide a decisive advantage, and my country should develop them.
Even with hostile regimes, dialogue usually works better than threats.
My country should be ready to start a war if that secures its vital interests.
My country should abolish its armed forces, as Costa Rica did.
Peace only exists when the enemy knows the response to an attack will be devastating.
The UN and international organizations should have more power to prevent wars.
No country has the right to try to change another country's government.
Pressuring other countries is legitimate when the national interest is at stake.
Military alliances end up dragging countries into wars that are not their own.
Foreign policy should pursue advantage, sovereignty, and influence, not international applause.
My country should not send soldiers abroad, not even on peacekeeping missions.
My country should use its weight to defend its companies abroad.
Even in the face of a genocide in a neighboring country, my country should not get involved militarily.
Sanctions and diplomatic pressure are legitimate when my country's interests are threatened.
Conflicts between countries should be resolved by international organizations, not by great powers.
My country should exercise political leadership over its region.
My country should avoid closed geopolitical blocs and permanent alliances.
Influencing neighboring governments is acceptable when it increases my country's security.
Each people should solve its own problems, without outside interference.
My country should use even military force to secure its interests in its region.
Embargoes and sanctions almost never work and end up punishing innocent civilians.
No international treaty should count for more than the national interest.
My country should remain neutral in wars, even under pressure from allies.
Countries that defend their interests firmly are more respected.
Keeping military bases in other countries is a waste of money.
If a neighboring country threatens its citizens or companies, my country should react harshly.
A revolution may be necessary to take economic power out of the hands of the few.
With competition, private companies provide better services than the state.
Strategic state-owned companies, such as the national oil company and postal service, should remain under public control.
Healthcare, education, and pensions should run mainly through private enterprise.
Factories, banks, and large companies should belong to the workers or to society, not to private owners.
Even roads, police, and courts could be private services, paid for by those who use them.
When the market excludes the poor, the state should take over the service directly.
Inheritance and family property must be protected from any redistribution project.
Healthcare, education, and water should not operate under the logic of profit.
Collecting taxes is, in the end, a form of theft.
A basic income paid to all citizens would be a civilizational advance.
Lifetime job security for civil servants makes the state rigid and expensive.
Large private companies concentrate too much power over people's lives.
Welfare programs create dependency when they last too long.
Land reform is still a necessary measure in my country.
Workers gain more by negotiating directly with their employer than through unions.
Public development banks are essential for the country's growth.
Private property must be respected even when it generates great inequality.
My country's privatizations sold public assets for far less than they were worth.
The state is almost always less efficient than the private sector.
The government should plan strategic sectors such as energy, housing, and industry.
The free market sets prices and wages better than any politician.
The central bank should obey the elected government, not act with total independence.
Companies should be able to hire, fire, and set prices with minimal interference.
Great fortunes should pay more taxes to fund public policies.
The lower the tax burden, the more the economy grows.
The state should subsidize strategic industries such as semiconductors, steel, and defense.
A minimum wage that is too high destroys jobs for the poorest.
In serious crises, the government should be able to freeze prices and rents.
Freezing prices by law causes shortages, queues, and black markets.
The government should choose and support national champion companies to compete abroad.
Cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin should be able to compete freely with government money.
An economy fully planned by the state would work better than the free market.
Every new regulation is, in the end, a hidden tax on those who produce.
In a recession, the government should spend more to restart the economy, even if it increases the debt.
An independent central bank is worth more than the current government's political wishes.
The government should be able to control exchange rates and money leaving the country to protect itself.
The central bank should be abolished, leaving money and interest rates to the market.
A minimum wage set by law protects workers more than free negotiation does.
Those who have money should be able to send it abroad without asking the government's permission.
National industry should be protected with tariffs whenever necessary.
Tariffs should be cut to almost zero, even if some national industries go bankrupt.
Too many imports destroy national industry and create unemployment.
Free trade agreements with other countries make the economy grow.
My country should produce domestically everything it consumes, even paying much more for it.
The more open to the world, the more innovation and quality reach the consumer.
The government should limit imports that threaten local industry and jobs.
The world would be better off without economic borders, working as a single global market.
Foreign companies should be banned from buying my country's strategic land and companies.
Trade blocs such as the European Union and Mercosur bring more gains than losses.
Food security means producing food in your own country, not depending on cheap imports.
Foreign investment creates jobs and brings technology to the country.
Purchases by the government and state companies should give priority to national companies.
International trade helps reduce poverty in every part of the world.
Cheap Chinese electric cars should pay tariffs to protect local factories.
Import tariffs in my country benefit a few business owners and make life more expensive for everyone.
Strategic supply chains, such as medicines and chips, should be protected from foreign competition.
Multinationals pay taxes, create jobs, and train local workers.
Economic sovereignty is worth more than low prices at the supermarket.
Globalization has raised the standard of living of most of humanity.
Religion is a personal matter and should not influence public policy.
Faith should be the guide for my moral and political choices.
Laws should be neutral and not follow the values of any religion.
The country's laws should reflect the values of the majority religion.
Churches and temples should pay taxes like any other organization.
Religion makes family life and life in the community stronger.
Public buildings, such as schools and courts, should not display religious symbols.
The state in my country should officially adopt a religious identity.
A society guided by science works better than one guided by faith.
Religious traditions should be preserved in the family and passed on to children.
In the end, humanity would be better off without any religion.
Pushing God out of public life caused part of today's moral problems.
Religious holidays should not be official in a secular state.
Marriage and family are sacred institutions, not just contracts.
The word 'God' should not appear in the constitution or on the currency.
Religion gives life a meaning that no philosophy can provide.
Teaching religion to young children is a form of indoctrination.
When the law of men contradicts the law of God, the law of God comes first.
You do not need to believe in God to be an ethical and good person.
Religious faith is part of the national identity and deserves protection.
Same-sex couples raise children just as well as couples of a man and a woman.
The traditional family and good customs should still guide society.
The gender identity declared by each person must be respected.
Cultural changes that come too fast end up destabilizing the whole of society.
Racial quotas correct a historical injustice and are still necessary.
Real marriage is between a man and a woman.
LGBT couples should be able to show affection in public like any other couple.
Racial quotas deepen division by color instead of overcoming it.
Abortion early in pregnancy can be a morally acceptable choice.
Abortion is wrong because it ends a human life.
Children and teenagers should learn about sexuality and gender without taboos.
Children's sex education should follow the family's values, not the school's.
Prostitution is a job like any other and deserves the same respect.
Gender-neutral language is an ideological imposition that distorts the language.
Reducing meat consumption out of respect for animals is a moral advance.
Pornography, prostitution, and drugs are signs of moral decay.
Open relationships and polyamory are choices as legitimate as traditional marriage.
A woman's most important role is caring for the family and the home.
Nudity in film, art, and on beaches should not scandalize anyone.
Parents should be the final authority in their children's moral education.
Nuclear energy, AI, and genetic engineering should be embraced without excessive fear.
Humanity would live better with less technology, in a simpler, more natural way of life.
AI and automation are welcome, even if they eliminate many of today's professions.
Technologies that alter the human body, mind, or reproduction should be blocked.
GMO crops have fed billions of people and should keep being developed.
Pesticides do more damage to the environment than they add to production.
It is possible to mine and extract resources from rainforests while keeping the forest standing.
Preserved nature is worth more than accelerated industrial growth.
Editing embryos' genes to create smarter, healthier people is a legitimate advance.
Global warming is an emergency and demands immediate changes in our way of life.
Exploring space and colonizing other planets is a natural destiny for humanity.
Even clean mining in untouched rainforests crosses a line that should not be crossed.
Life in big cities offers more opportunities than life in the countryside.
Editing embryos to choose intelligence or looks crosses an ethical line.
Brain implants and prosthetics to expand human capacities are a legitimate path.
Solving Earth's problems comes before spending billions on space.
Lab-grown meat is an advance that can replace livestock farming.
The simple life of the countryside is healthier than life in big cities.
Against global warming, relying on technology makes more sense than cutting consumption.
The human body should not be enhanced with chips and artificial modifications.
